user_goal.namespace:
Durable goals the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> is working toward. Create a goal when the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> is
working toward an enduring outcome, behavior, or area of life. Recognize
durable goals even when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user never<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->nobody<!-- group-only:end --> says "goal": repeated aspirations,
progress updates, setbacks, commitments with a timeframe, or asking for help
with a whole area of life. Not goals: fleeting todos, one-time reminders,
minor updates that belong on an existing goal, or work you carry for the
<!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> (that is the tracking namespace). Clarify one question at a time.
Clarify the outcome the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> wants when it is unclear.
Offer practical help. Raise a goal only when
relevant to the current conversation, and log milestone wins that same turn
without derailing the topic.

Use the list, search, and get functions to resolve goal identity before
creating or updating. Search matches terms across goal ids, titles,
`current_state`, and descriptions and returns lifecycle state and
timestamps.

Every set_status call requires a concise <!-- personal-only:start -->user-facing `reason`<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->`reason`, written for members,<!-- group-only:end --> explaining the
transition.

Each existing goal has a workspace at `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/`; before
updating or helping with an existing goal, read its `GOAL.md`
first. `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` is your own notes on the goal
rather than a document for <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->members<!-- group-only:end -->. Write in
<!-- personal-only:start -->
`workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` where the goal stands now, the user's
<!-- personal-only:end -->
<!-- group-only:start -->
`workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` where the goal stands now, the group's and members'
<!-- group-only:end -->
constraints on the goal such as schedule, injuries, budget, or boundaries,
the facts you learned while setting the goal up, and the current shape of
the plan. Update `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` with the file tools
when you finish setting a goal up, when a constraint or the plan changes,
and when helping with the goal reveals information worth keeping. When a goal is
created, the runtime seeds `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` with a
header carrying the goal's title, id, slug, and description. The runtime
does not write to `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` again. All of
`workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md` is yours to edit, the seeded header
included. Renaming or recategorizing a goal updates the goal record but not
`workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md`, so the seeded header can go stale.
When the seeded header and the goal record disagree, trust the goal record
from `user_goal.get`. Record progress with `create_entry` even when you have already
written that progress into `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/GOAL.md`.
Documents <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> asked for go in `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/files/`,
<!-- personal-only:start -->which the user sees as <!-- personal-only:end -->the goal's documents; check logs, watermarks,
snapshots, and other bookkeeping go in
`workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/hidden_files/`, which <!-- personal-only:start -->the user does<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->members do<!-- group-only:end --> not see. Do
not add unrequested files under `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/files/` or
`workspace/your_files/`: record progress with `create_entry`, not as a new
document. When helping with an existing goal in a later conversation, read
`~/skills/goals/SKILL.md` and that goal category's scaffold at
`~/skills/goals/guides/<category>/scaffold.md`. The goal record carries the
category, so confirm with `user_goal.get` before concluding a goal has none.
When the record's own category is absent, read
`~/skills/goals/SKILL.md` alone.

get.description:
Read one <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal by its exact `goal_id`. Returns the goal's metadata (title, `current_state` pulse, description, lifecycle status, category - `null` for an uncategorized record - and parent linkage), its full timeline of dated activity entries, and its suggestions, associations, and briefings. When you do not know the id, find it with `user_goal.list` or `user_goal.search` first.

Each goal has a workspace at `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/`; read its `GOAL.md` before doing anything substantial related to the goal. Timeline entries carry an `update_id`, which `user_goal.update_entry` and `user_goal.delete_entry` take.
get.short: Read one <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal by id: metadata plus its activity timeline, suggestions, associations, and briefings. When you do not know the id, find it with user_goal.list or user_goal.search first.

list.description:
List the <!-- personal-only:start -->user's<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group's<!-- group-only:end --> own goals. Returns up to `limit` goals (default 100) with each goal's id, title, `current_state` (the one-line status pulse), description, lifecycle status, category (`null` for an uncategorized record), timestamps, and parent linkage, plus any storage warnings. Goals here are the <!-- personal-only:start -->user's<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group's<!-- group-only:end --> durable aspirations and commitments. Work you track for the <!-- personal-only:start -->user on their<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group on its<!-- group-only:end --> behalf is a separate surface and never appears here; list that with `tracking.list`.

Use it to resolve goal identity before mutating: check whether an aspiration already has a goal before creating one with `user_goal.create`, and confirm the exact `goal_id` before calling `user_goal.update`, `user_goal.set_status`, or `user_goal.create_entry`. For a keyword lookup across a long roster use `user_goal.search`; for one goal's full timeline use `user_goal.get`.
list.short: List the <!-- personal-only:start -->user's<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group's<!-- group-only:end --> own goals: id, title, current state, lifecycle status, and parent linkage. Use it to resolve goal identity before creating or updating. Work you track for the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> lives in tracking.list instead.

create.description:
For a new goal, your first response is conversational - never a create call - unless the opening message already carries concrete specifics (a target, baseline, deadline, or success condition): brief intake first, then one created record, and only then durable support. Create a goal when the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> is working toward an enduring outcome, <!-- personal-only:start -->behavior<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->shared habit<!-- group-only:end -->, or area of <!-- personal-only:start -->life<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->its life together<!-- group-only:end -->. Recognize durable goals even when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user never<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->no member<!-- group-only:end --> says goal: repeated aspirations, progress updates, setbacks, commitments with a timeframe, or asking for help with a whole area of life. Not goals: fleeting todos, one-time reminders, minor updates that belong on an existing goal, or work you carry for the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> (that is `tracking.create`). Clarify one question at a time<!-- group-only:start -->,<!-- group-only:end --> and clarify the outcome the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> wants when it is unclear. Offer practical help. Raise a goal only when relevant to the current conversation.

A goal-creation contract may already be injected into this conversation<!-- personal-only:start --> (the Goals tab does this automatically)<!-- personal-only:end -->. When it is, that injected contract is the complete creation guide: run intake and create the goal directly from it, with zero guidance reads - the goals skill files add nothing to the injected contract, and a read only delays your first question. Only when no goal-creation contract for this new goal's category is in context, read `~/skills/goals/creation/<category>.md` before intake. Choose the category from the life-area `category` values this tool accepts; when none fits, read `~/skills/goals/creation/something_else.md`. Account connections, builds, and monitoring are offered only after the record exists, and built only <!-- personal-only:start -->on the user's confirmation - never silently. Offer a connection as a widget with a "Not now" option, never as a raw link in prose<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->once a member confirms. Offer a connection by posting its connect link in the group with a short note on what it adds<!-- group-only:end -->.

Before creating, resolve identity with `user_goal.list` or `user_goal.search`: when the aspiration matches an existing goal, log progress to it with `user_goal.create_entry` instead, and when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> explicitly restarts a completed goal, reopen it with `user_goal.set_status`; never create a replacement.

Give the goal a `title` that is a concise noun phrase naming the goal itself, a one-line `current_state` pulse, and a two or three sentence `description`; detailed progress belongs in activity entries. Optionally nest it under a top-level <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal with `parent_goal_id`, pick a life-area `category`, and classify it with `goal_kind` and `value_alignment`<!-- personal-only:start -->. When the user is creating from the app's goal creation flow, a missing `category` is filled from the area they chose there<!-- personal-only:end -->. Creation returns the new goal immediately, including its `goal_id`, and sets up its workspace at `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/`. When helping with an existing goal in a later conversation, read `~/skills/goals/SKILL.md` and that goal category's scaffold at `~/skills/goals/guides/<category>/scaffold.md`. The goal record carries the category, so confirm with `user_goal.get` before concluding a goal has none. When the record's own category is absent, read `~/skills/goals/SKILL.md` alone.
create.short: Create a durable goal the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> is working toward: an enduring aspiration, commitment, or <!-- group-only:start -->shared <!-- group-only:end -->area of life, even when <!-- personal-only:start -->they never say<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->no member says<!-- group-only:end --> goal. Not for fleeting todos or work you carry for <!-- personal-only:start -->them<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->the group<!-- group-only:end --> (tracking.create). For a new goal, your first response is conversational - never a create call - unless the opening message already carries concrete specifics (a target, baseline, deadline, or success condition): brief intake first, then one created record, and only then support or any account or data connection.

delete.description:
Permanently delete a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal by `goal_id`, removing it and its activity timeline from the <!-- personal-only:start -->user's<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group's<!-- group-only:end --> goals. Files from the goal's workspace are preserved on disk, and the response lists their paths.

Deletion is for mistakes and for goals <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> explicitly asks to remove. A goal the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> finished, achieved, or abandoned should instead be completed with `user_goal.set_status`, which keeps its history visible. Confirm the exact `goal_id` with `user_goal.list` or `user_goal.search` first.
delete.short: Permanently delete a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal and its timeline. For a goal that ended, prefer user_goal.set_status completed; delete only mistakes or goals <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> asks to remove.

search.description:
Search the <!-- personal-only:start -->user's<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group's<!-- group-only:end --> goals with keyword terms. Terms match case-insensitively against each goal's id, title, `current_state`, and description, across every lifecycle state including completed goals. Results are ranked by how many terms match, then by most recent update, and come back as compact projections with lifecycle status, category (`null` for an uncategorized record), and timestamps plus a total `match_count`. The `query` needs at least one term of two or more characters; `limit` defaults to 10 (maximum 100).

Prefer this over `user_goal.list` when the roster is long and you are hunting for one specific goal, including checking whether a past or completed goal already covers what <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> just described. Work you track for the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> is a separate surface; search that with `tracking.search`.
search.short: Search the <!-- personal-only:start -->user's<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group's<!-- group-only:end --> goals by keywords across id, title, current state, and description, including completed goals. Prefer this over user_goal.list to find one specific goal in a long roster.

update.description:
Update a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal's metadata: `title`, `current_state`, `description`, `category`, `goal_kind`, `value_alignment`, parent linkage, or <!-- personal-only:start -->brief pushes<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->proactive briefs<!-- group-only:end -->. Provide the `goal_id` plus only the fields you are changing. Use it only for an explicit correction that is not already represented by a new activity entry, and do not append a generic next step to the state line. New progress, results, or events belong on the timeline via `user_goal.create_entry` (the runtime refreshes `current_state` from entries itself), and lifecycle changes belong to `user_goal.set_status`.

Use `parent_goal_id` to move the goal under a new top-level <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal, or pass an empty string to detach it to top level. Set `pushable` to false when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user says<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member asks<!-- group-only:end --> to stop proactive <!-- personal-only:start -->brief pushes for this goal; briefs still show when they read the Goals tab<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->briefs about this goal<!-- group-only:end -->. Find the exact `goal_id` with `user_goal.list` or `user_goal.search`.
update.short: Correct a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal's metadata: title, description, state line, parent, category, kind, or <!-- personal-only:start -->brief pushes<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->proactive briefs<!-- group-only:end -->. For new progress use user_goal.create_entry; to complete or reopen the goal use user_goal.set_status.

set_status.description:
Set a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal's lifecycle to active or completed, with a required <!-- personal-only:start -->user-facing<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->plain-language<!-- group-only:end --> `reason` explaining the transition. This is the complete lifecycle: active means the goal remains open, completed means it ended.

Complete a goal when the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> reaches it, ends it, or clearly moves on from it. Use active only to reopen the existing completed goal when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> explicitly restarts that responsibility; never create a replacement goal with `user_goal.create`. The change may also record a closing or reopening entry on the goal's timeline; the response says whether anything changed and includes any recorded entry. Find the `goal_id` with `user_goal.list` or `user_goal.search`.
set_status.short: Complete or reopen a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal with a <!-- personal-only:start -->user-facing<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->plain-language<!-- group-only:end --> reason. Complete when the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> finishes or drops the goal; use active only when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> explicitly restarts it, never create a replacement goal.

create_entry.description:
Add one activity entry to a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal's timeline. Log an entry when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> reports progress, a result, a setback, a milestone, or a decision that moves or changes the goal; log milestone wins the same turn they happen without derailing the conversation. Keep the entry concise and <!-- personal-only:start -->user-facing<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->in plain words<!-- group-only:end -->, say what happened and any result, and record each activity once.

The runtime reads each new entry and replaces the goal's `current_state` pulse when the activity supports a newer or more useful current or forward-looking status, and otherwise preserves it. Do not make a separate `user_goal.update` call for that state decision. An entry on a nested goal is also rolled up onto its parent goal's timeline automatically. Use `effective_at` when logging something that happened earlier than now; it accepts RFC 3339 timestamps or YYYY-MM-DD and defaults to now.

Find the goal's `goal_id` with `user_goal.list` or `user_goal.search`, or create the goal first with `user_goal.create`.
create_entry.short: Log one activity entry on a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal's timeline when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> reports progress, a setback, a milestone, or a decision. The runtime refreshes the goal's state line itself; entries on subgoals also land on the parent.

delete_entry.description:
Delete one activity entry from a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal's timeline by its `update_id`, taken from the timeline `user_goal.get` returns. The response echoes the deleted entry's id, goal, and title.

Use it to remove a duplicate or mistaken entry. It does not touch the goal itself or recompute the goal's `current_state`; correct a wrong entry with `user_goal.update_entry` instead of deleting and re-adding, and delete a whole goal with `user_goal.delete`.
delete_entry.short: Delete one activity entry from a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal's timeline by its update id (from user_goal.get). To remove the whole goal use user_goal.delete.

update_entry.description:
Edit one existing activity entry on a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal's timeline. Provide the entry's `update_id` (from the timeline `user_goal.get` returns) plus at least one of `title`, `current_state`, `description`, or `effective_at`; a call changing none of them is rejected. Use it to fix wording, correct the outcome line, or move the entry to when the activity actually happened. Keep the entry concise and <!-- personal-only:start -->user-facing<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->in plain words<!-- group-only:end -->, saying what happened and, when applicable, what the result was.

This edits the entry in place; it does not re-run the state decision that `user_goal.create_entry` triggers. For new activity add a new entry with `user_goal.create_entry` instead, and to remove an entry use `user_goal.delete_entry`.
update_entry.short: Edit one existing activity entry on a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal's timeline: fix its title, text, outcome line, or effective time. Takes the entry's update id from user_goal.get.

delete_briefing.description: Delete one stored briefing from a <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal, including its briefing HTML and associated hero image. Historical delivery and engagement records are retained. Use the exact briefing_id returned by user_goal.get. This does not delete the goal or its other activity.
delete_briefing.short: Use when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> asks to delete, remove, or forget one specific goal briefing while keeping the goal itself.

fields.get.goal_id: Exact goal id, as returned by user_goal.list, user_goal.search, or user_goal.create.
fields.list.offset: Use next_offset from the previous page; omit for the first page.
fields.list.limit: Maximum number of goals to return. Defaults to 100.
fields.create.title: <!-- personal-only:start -->Concise user-facing noun phrase<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->Concise, readable noun phrase<!-- group-only:end --> naming the goal itself, not an instruction. Avoid generic leading verbs like `Track ...`; use concrete domain wording (`Marathon under four hours`, `Career change to product design`). Current activity and status go in current_state.
fields.create.current_state: <!-- personal-only:start -->The one-line user-facing state<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->The one-line plain-language state<!-- group-only:end -->. Write one short pulse from the newest evidence that states the single most useful current or forward-looking status: a result, progress marker, specific wait, blocker, monitored condition, or scheduled event. Do not claim work is currently in progress, append a generic next step, or restate the title or description.
fields.create.description: <!-- personal-only:start -->Two or three natural, user-facing sentences<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->Two or three natural, plain-language sentences<!-- group-only:end --> that explain the goal at a high level. Put detailed progress and state changes in activity entries instead.
fields.create.emoji: Single emoji for the goal. Defaults to a generic goal emoji when omitted.
fields.create.parent_goal_id: Id of an existing TOP-LEVEL <!-- personal-only:start -->user goal<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group goal<!-- group-only:end --> to nest this one under. The parent must itself be a <!-- personal-only:start -->user goal<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group goal<!-- group-only:end -->, not assistant-tracked work.
fields.create.value_alignment: <!-- personal-only:start -->Short user-facing note on why this goal matters to the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->Short plain-language note on why this goal matters to the group<!-- group-only:end -->.
fields.delete.goal_id: Goal id, as returned by user_goal.list, user_goal.search, or user_goal.create.
fields.search.query: Terms to match against goal id, title, current_state, and description. At least one term of two or more characters.
fields.search.limit: Maximum number of matches to return. Defaults to 10.
fields.update.parent_goal_id: Id of a TOP-LEVEL <!-- personal-only:start -->user goal<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group goal<!-- group-only:end --> to move this goal under. Pass an empty string to detach the goal to top level.
fields.update.pushable: <!-- personal-only:start -->Set false when the user says to stop proactive brief pushes for this goal; briefs still show in the Goals tab. Set true to resume pushes<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->Set false when a member asks to stop proactive briefs about this goal. Set true to resume them<!-- group-only:end -->.
fields.set_status.status: The complete lifecycle for <!-- personal-only:start -->user goals<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group goals<!-- group-only:end -->: active means the goal remains open, completed means it ended.
fields.set_status.reason: <!-- personal-only:start -->Concise user-facing explanation<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->Concise plain-language explanation<!-- group-only:end --> of why the lifecycle changed. Required.
fields.goal_kind: outcome = result to achieve. behavior = action pattern to adopt. learning = skill to acquire (spaced study). habit = recurring practice. maintenance = hold a standard. recovery = return from a setback. identity = who <!-- personal-only:start -->the user wants<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->members want<!-- group-only:end --> to become. exploratory = open-ended discovery.
fields.create_entry.title: <!-- personal-only:start -->Concise user-facing title<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->Concise, readable title<!-- group-only:end --> for this activity entry.
fields.create_entry.current_state: State the activity's main outcome in one line.
fields.create_entry.description: One concise, human-friendly sentence about what happened and, when applicable, what the result was.
fields.create_entry.effective_at: When the activity actually happened. Accepts RFC 3339 timestamps or YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to now.
fields.delete_entry.update_id: Activity entry id, from the timeline user_goal.get returns.
fields.delete_briefing.briefing_id: Exact briefing id returned in a user_goal.get briefing record.
fields.category: Life area for the goal. The value stays on the goal record as the goal's category. A creation turn reads that category's guide at ~/skills/goals/creation/<category>.md. A coaching turn reads that category's scaffold at ~/skills/goals/guides/<category>/scaffold.md.<!-- personal-only:start --> When the user is creating from the app's goal creation flow and this is omitted, the area they chose there is used.<!-- personal-only:end -->

extra.update.escalation: `escalation` is what to do if a stated condition is not met by a date: `{condition, due_at, action}` with `action` `notify` (tell the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end -->) or `ask` (the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> must decide next). Set it only from something <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> said, a conditional follow-up or a hard deadline with a consequence they named, and only after they confirm it; pass `null` to clear one <!-- personal-only:start -->they have<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->the group has<!-- group-only:end --> withdrawn. Omitting it leaves the stored value alone.
extra.shared.set_status: For a shared goal, include `host_hamlet` and the `expected_revision` from `user_goal.get`. The host changes the shared status only if that revision is still current.
extra.shared.update: For a shared goal, include `host_hamlet` and the `expected_revision` from `user_goal.get`. You can change its title, current state, description, or a task. A new task needs a task ID, title, and `assigned_to` Hamlet ID. Use `completed` to record progress, or `remove_task` to remove it. The host applies the edit to the shared record. If the revision changed, read the returned state before trying again.
extra.shared.get: For a shared goal, include `host_hamlet` from the shared item. Use `host_hamlet: "self"` for a shared goal this Hamlet hosts, including one you just created in a connection conversation. The host returns the current title, state, tasks, assignments, progress by participant, and revision. Read this view before adding tasks or changing a shared goal. Omit `host_hamlet` for ordinary goal details, category, timeline, and briefings.
extra.shared.fields.expected_revision: The revision from the latest shared goal read.
extra.shared.fields.mutation_id: Reuse this ID when retrying the same shared goal change.
extra.shared.fields.task_id: The shared task to edit, or a new UUID for a new task.

tracked item before scheduling a call, cron, heartbeat check, or other

get.description:
Read one tracked work item in full by its `goal_id`. Returns the item's metadata (title, `current_state` pulse, description, lifecycle status, parent linkage) together with its complete activity timeline, plus any pending suggestions, associations, and recent briefings. Each timeline entry carries its `update_id`, title, outcome line, description, and effective time; those `update_id` values are what `tracking.update_entry` and `tracking.delete_entry` take.

Each tracked item also has a workspace directory at `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/`; read its `GOAL.md` before doing any substantial work related to the item. When you do not know the `goal_id`, find it with `tracking.list` or `tracking.search` first.
get.short: Read one tracked work item by id: metadata plus its full activity timeline and briefings. When you do not know the id, find it with tracking.list or tracking.search first.

list.description:
List the work items you are tracking for the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end -->. Returns up to `limit` items (default 100) with each item's id, title, `current_state` (the one-line status pulse), description, lifecycle status, timestamps, and parent linkage, plus any storage warnings. Items here are assistant-tracked responsibilities: monitoring, follow-ups, background work, and other work you carry across turns on the <!-- personal-only:start -->user's<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group's<!-- group-only:end --> behalf. The <!-- personal-only:start -->user's<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group's<!-- group-only:end --> own goals are a separate surface and never appear here.

Use it to resolve identity before mutating: check whether a responsibility already has a tracked item before creating one with `tracking.create`, and confirm the exact `goal_id` before calling `tracking.update`, `tracking.set_status`, or `tracking.create_entry`. For a keyword lookup across a long roster use `tracking.search`; for one item's full timeline use `tracking.get`.
list.short: List the work items the assistant is tracking for the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end -->: monitoring, follow-ups, background work. Use it to resolve item identity before creating, updating, or logging to a tracked item.

create.description:
Create a tracked item for a concrete plan, commitment, or outcome the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> cares about beyond the immediate conversation, such as a reservation, delivery, reminder, trip, or ongoing project. Track it even when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user does not say<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->no member says<!-- group-only:end --> "track this" or the next step is quick. Keep it open while the relevant event, delivery, or follow-up is still pending, even if booking or checkout is complete. Skip ordinary conversation and requests whose outcome is fully resolved in the current turn. Associate the work with its tracked item before scheduling a call, cron, heartbeat check, or other background mechanism. For a <!-- personal-only:start -->user-requested reminder<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->reminder a member requested<!-- group-only:end -->, record the scheduled time as when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->it<!-- group-only:end --> is due and close the item once the reminder is delivered and nothing remains owed.

Before creating, resolve identity with `tracking.list` or `tracking.search`: when the work belongs to an existing tracked item, log to that item with `tracking.create_entry` instead, and when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> explicitly restarts a completed responsibility, reopen that item with `tracking.set_status`; never create a replacement instance. An active <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal is such an existing record: when the work serves one of the <!-- personal-only:start -->user's<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group's<!-- group-only:end --> existing goals (accountability, check-ins, nudges, monitoring, or reminders for that goal's outcome), it belongs on that goal as goal-owned schedules and timeline entries, never as a new tracked item, subgoal, or second goal record shadowing the goal. Attach the cron or check-in to that goal (cron owner `goal:<goal-slug>`) and log progress with `user_goal.create_entry`.

Give the item a `title` that is a concise noun phrase naming the work itself, a one-line `current_state` pulse, and a two or three sentence `description`; detailed progress belongs in activity entries, not the description. Optionally nest it under a top-level tracked item with `parent_goal_id`, and classify it with `goal_kind` and `value_alignment`. Creation returns the new item immediately, including its `goal_id`. Each created item gets a workspace at `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/` with a `GOAL.md`; read that file before doing later work on the item.
create.short: Track a concrete plan, commitment, or outcome the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> cares about beyond the immediate conversation: reservations, deliveries, reminders, trips, or ongoing projects. Create an item when no existing goal record represents it. Attach work serving an existing <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> goal to that goal instead. Create before scheduling a call or other background mechanism; log progress with tracking.create_entry.

delete.description:
Permanently delete a tracked work item by `goal_id`, removing it and its activity timeline from the tracked-work roster. Files from the item's `workspace/goals/<goal-slug>/` directory are preserved on disk, and the response lists the preserved paths.

Deleting is for mistakes and for items <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> explicitly asks to remove. When the responsibility simply ended (shipped, event over, target reached, window expired, <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->the group<!-- group-only:end --> cancelled), close it with `tracking.set_status` completed instead so the record and its history stay available. To remove a single wrong timeline entry rather than the whole item, use `tracking.delete_entry`.
delete.short: Permanently delete a tracked work item and its timeline. For work that simply ended, prefer tracking.set_status completed; delete only mistakes or items <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> asks to remove.

search.description:
Search your tracked work items with keyword terms. Terms match case-insensitively against each item's id, title, `current_state`, and description; words shorter than two characters are ignored, and the query must contain at least one term of two or more characters. Matches cover every lifecycle state, so completed items are found too. Results are ranked by how many terms match, then by most recent update, and return compact projections (long text fields are cut at 2,000 characters) with lifecycle status, timestamps, and parent linkage, plus the total match count. Returns at most `limit` matches (default 10, maximum 100).

Use it to resolve whether a responsibility already has a tracked item before creating a new one with `tracking.create`, and to find ids for `tracking.get`, `tracking.update`, or `tracking.set_status`. For a plain bounded roster with full text use `tracking.list` instead.
search.short: Search tracked work items by keywords across id, title, current state, and description, including completed items. Prefer this over tracking.list to find one specific responsibility in a long roster.

update.description:
Patch a tracked work item's metadata by `goal_id`: title, `current_state`, description, parent linkage, `goal_kind`, or `value_alignment`. Only the fields you pass change. Use it only for an explicit correction that is not already represented by new activity: when something happened, log it with `tracking.create_entry` instead, and the runtime refreshes the item's `current_state` pulse from that entry on its own. Do not make an update call solely to restate progress or append a generic next step.

Lifecycle is not editable here; open or complete the item with `tracking.set_status`. `parent_goal_id` moves the item under a new parent, which must be a top-level tracked item; pass an empty string to detach the item to top-level. The target must be an assistant-tracked item; this tool cannot edit the <!-- personal-only:start -->user's<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group's<!-- group-only:end --> own goals. Find the exact `goal_id` with `tracking.list` or `tracking.search`.
update.short: Correct a tracked item's metadata: title, description, state line, parent, or kind. For new progress or events use tracking.create_entry; to open or complete the item use tracking.set_status.

set_status.description:
Set a tracked work item's lifecycle to active or completed, with a required <!-- personal-only:start -->user-facing<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->plain-language<!-- group-only:end --> `reason` explaining the transition. This is the complete lifecycle: active means the responsibility remains open, completed means it ended.

Close tracked items proactively when the best available evidence shows the responsibility ended; do not wait for <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member to ask<!-- group-only:end -->. Use conversation history, completed work or tool results, reliable real-world facts, and current time relative to known dates. Respect an explicit stop immediately. Examples: delivery received; event ended; target reached; window expired; <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->the group<!-- group-only:end --> cancelled. Silence or one finished step alone is not enough. Use active only to reopen the existing completed item when <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> explicitly restarts the responsibility; never create a replacement item with `tracking.create`.

The change runs through the daemon's tracking lifecycle coordinator, which may also record a closing or reopening activity entry; the response says whether anything changed and includes any recorded entry. Find the `goal_id` with `tracking.list` or `tracking.search`.
set_status.short: Complete or reopen a tracked work item, with a <!-- personal-only:start -->user-facing<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->plain-language<!-- group-only:end --> reason. Close proactively when evidence shows the responsibility ended; reopen the same item instead of creating a replacement.

create_entry.description:
Add one activity entry to a tracked item's timeline. Log activity incrementally whenever anything happens on tracked work, including a step starting or completing, a check, new or confirmed information, deliverable progress, an artifact change, a result, checkpoint, check-in, feedback, direction change, blocker, schedule change, or lifecycle change. Do not wait for a milestone or material change. Keep the entry concise and <!-- personal-only:start -->user-facing<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->in plain words<!-- group-only:end -->, say what happened and any result, and record each activity once.

The runtime reads each new entry and replaces the item's `current_state` pulse when the activity supports a newer or more useful current or forward-looking status, and otherwise preserves it; it also refreshes the item's attention state. Do not make a separate `tracking.update` call for that state decision. An entry on a nested item is also rolled up onto its parent's timeline automatically. Use `effective_at` when logging something that happened earlier than now; it accepts RFC 3339 timestamps or `YYYY-MM-DD` and defaults to now.

An entry does not change lifecycle status. When the whole tracked responsibility has ended, close the item with `tracking.set_status` in the same turn.

Find the item's `goal_id` with `tracking.list` or `tracking.search`, or create the item first with `tracking.create`.
create_entry.short: Log activity on a tracked item's timeline whenever anything happens: a step, check, result, blocker, or schedule change. Log incrementally; do not wait for milestones. The runtime refreshes the item's state line itself. An entry does not close the item; use tracking.set_status when the whole responsibility ends.

delete_entry.description:
Delete one activity entry from a tracked item's timeline by its `update_id` (from the timeline `tracking.get` returns). The response confirms the deleted entry's id, its item's `goal_id`, and its title.

This removes only the single entry; the tracked item itself and the rest of its history stay. To fix a wrong entry instead of removing it, use `tracking.update_entry`. To remove the whole item use `tracking.delete`, and to close finished work use `tracking.set_status`.
delete_entry.short: Delete one activity entry from a tracked item's timeline by its update id (from tracking.get). To remove the whole item use tracking.delete.

update_entry.description:
Edit an existing activity entry on a tracked item's timeline. Pass the entry's `update_id` (from the timeline `tracking.get` returns) and at least one of `title`, `current_state`, `description`, or `effective_at`; omitted fields keep their current values, and any field you pass must be non-empty. Keep the entry concise and <!-- personal-only:start -->user-facing<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->in plain words<!-- group-only:end -->, saying what happened and, when applicable, what the result was. `current_state` states the activity's main outcome in one line. `effective_at` accepts RFC 3339 timestamps or `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Editing an entry also triggers a refresh of the tracked item's attention state. Use this only to correct an entry that is already recorded; new activity gets its own `tracking.create_entry` call, and item-level metadata corrections go through `tracking.update`.
update_entry.short: Edit one existing activity entry on a tracked item's timeline: fix its title, text, outcome line, or effective time. Takes the entry's update id from tracking.get.

fields.get.goal_id: Exact tracked item id to read. Tracked item id, as returned by tracking.list, tracking.search, or tracking.create.
fields.list.offset: Use next_offset from the previous page; omit for the first page.
fields.list.limit: Maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 100.
fields.create.title: <!-- personal-only:start -->Concise user-facing noun phrase<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->Concise, readable noun phrase<!-- group-only:end --> naming the tracked work itself, not an instruction. Avoid generic leading verbs like `Track ...`; use concrete domain wording (`Wimbledon daily analysis`, `Childcare coordination`). Current activity and status go in current_state.
fields.create.current_state: <!-- personal-only:start -->The one-line user-facing state<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->The one-line plain-language state<!-- group-only:end -->. Write one short pulse from the newest evidence that states the single most useful current or forward-looking status: a result, progress marker, specific wait, blocker, monitored condition, or scheduled event. Do not claim work is currently in progress, append a generic next step, or restate the title or description.
fields.create.description: <!-- personal-only:start -->Two or three natural, user-facing sentences<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->Two or three natural, plain-language sentences<!-- group-only:end --> that explain the tracked work at a high level. Put detailed progress and state changes in activity entries instead.
fields.create.emoji: Single emoji for the item. Defaults to a generic goal emoji when omitted.
fields.create.parent_goal_id: Id of an existing TOP-LEVEL tracked item to nest this one under. The parent must itself be assistant-tracked work, not a <!-- personal-only:start -->user goal<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group goal<!-- group-only:end -->.
fields.create.value_alignment: <!-- personal-only:start -->Short user-facing note on why this work matters to the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->Short plain-language note on why this work matters to the group<!-- group-only:end -->.
fields.delete.goal_id: Tracked item id to delete permanently. Tracked item id, as returned by tracking.list, tracking.search, or tracking.create.
fields.search.query: Terms to match against tracked item id, title, current_state, and description. Words shorter than two characters are ignored; at least one longer term is required.
fields.search.limit: Maximum matches to return. Defaults to 10.
fields.update.goal_id: Tracked item id, as returned by tracking.list, tracking.search, or tracking.create.
fields.update.current_state: <!-- personal-only:start -->The one-line user-facing state<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->The one-line plain-language state<!-- group-only:end -->. Write one short pulse from the newest evidence that states the single most useful current or forward-looking status: a result, progress marker, specific wait, blocker, monitored condition, or scheduled event. Do not claim work is currently in progress, append a generic next step, or restate the title or description. Use update only for an explicit correction that is not already represented by a new activity entry.
fields.update.parent_goal_id: Move the item under a new parent, which must be a top-level tracked item. Pass an empty string to detach the item to top-level.
fields.set_status.status: The complete lifecycle for tracked work: active means the responsibility remains open, completed means it ended.
fields.set_status.reason: <!-- personal-only:start -->Concise user-facing explanation<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->Concise plain-language explanation<!-- group-only:end --> of why the lifecycle changed. Required.
fields.goal_kind: outcome = result to achieve. behavior = action pattern to adopt. learning = skill to acquire. habit = recurring practice. maintenance = hold a standard. recovery = return from a setback. identity = who <!-- personal-only:start -->the user wants<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->members want<!-- group-only:end --> to become. exploratory = open-ended discovery.
fields.create_entry.title: <!-- personal-only:start -->Concise user-facing title<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->Concise, readable title<!-- group-only:end --> for this activity entry.
fields.create_entry.current_state: State the activity's main outcome in one line.
fields.create_entry.description: One concise, human-friendly sentence about what happened and, when applicable, what the result was.
fields.create_entry.effective_at: When the activity actually happened. Accepts RFC 3339 timestamps or YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to now.
fields.delete_entry.update_id: Activity entry id, from the timeline tracking.get returns.
fields.update_entry.effective_at: When the activity actually happened. Accepts RFC 3339 timestamps or YYYY-MM-DD.

extra.watch:
Set `watch` to start a private session the moment something arrives, instead of checking for it on a schedule. Name the connected source and the exact thing to wait for in it, such as an email thread or a sender, a calendar event, a chat, an order or a place. Add a short note saying what you will do when it arrives.

A watch lives on this tracked item and ends with it. Clear it with `tracking.update` when the wait is over. A private session cannot change a watch the user asked for, so it says in its handoff that the wait is over, and the main conversation clears it.

A watch matches only what arrives from sources the user has connected and allowed you to read in the background. It does not make a source sync more often. An arrival is noticed the next time that source syncs, which is about hourly in waking hours. A place is noticed as the user's phone crosses into it, when the phone is connected and allowed to share location in the background.

Use a one-off `cron.add` instead when the thing happens at a known time, such as a check-in after an appointment.
extra.watch.clear: Set `watch` to null to clear it.
extra.requested: Set `requested` when the user asked to be told. A requested watch keeps working when the user turns proactive work off, the way a scheduled task they set up does. A watch you set on your own stops with the rest.
extra.watch.target.connector: The connected source it arrives from. Leave it out for a place.
extra.watch.target.thread_id: For an email thread, the thread ID its connector returned.
extra.watch.target.address: For a sender, their email address.
extra.watch.target.event_id: For a calendar event, its event ID.
extra.watch.target.chat_id: For a chat, the chat ID its connector returned.
extra.watch.target.node_id: For a place, the node ID of the phone that watches it.
extra.watch.target.region_id: For a place, the ID the phone's `geofence.set` returned through `device.invoke`.
extra.update.escalation: `escalation` is what to do if a stated condition is not met by a date: `{condition, due_at, action}` with `action` `notify` (tell the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end -->) or `ask` (the <!-- personal-only:start -->user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->group<!-- group-only:end --> must decide next). Set it only from something <!-- personal-only:start -->the user<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->a member<!-- group-only:end --> said, a conditional follow-up or a hard deadline with a consequence they named, and only after they confirm it; pass `null` to clear one <!-- personal-only:start -->they have<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->the group has<!-- group-only:end --> withdrawn. Omitting it leaves the stored value alone.
extra.connection_id.create: The conversation coordinating this work, from connection.get. A private reference to someone is not enough to link it. Linking directs follow-ups; it does not share the record. Omission uses the current connection when working in a connection's scope; otherwise it leaves the item independent. Null keeps the item independent.
extra.connection_id.update: The conversation coordinating this work, from connection.get. A private reference to someone is not enough to link it. Linking directs follow-ups; it does not share the record. Omit to preserve the link; null removes it.
extra.connection_id.list: Filter by the conversation coordinating this work. Omit to list <!-- personal-only:start -->your user's private tracking<!-- personal-only:end --><!-- group-only:start -->the group's tracking<!-- group-only:end --> across conversations.
extra.follow_up_at: Next private check, as RFC 3339, separate from the task deadline. A new link gets one initial check if omitted. On update, omit to preserve the schedule. Use null to wait for a reply or new evidence. Do not rearm just to repeat an unanswered nudge.

texts.goal_not_exists: {goal_id} does not exist. It may have been deleted or it may have never existed. In either case you are UNABLE to update or edit this goal and must inform the user the goal they referred to does not exist. Do not share or repeat the internal goal_id to the user; refer to the goal by the user's goal name or request topic when available. You can suggest creating a new goal on the request topic.
texts.query_too_short: query must contain at least one term with two or more characters; use {ns}.list to browse records without a search term
texts.watch_not_saved: The item was created, but its watch was not saved ({error}). Set it with `tracking.update`.
texts.parent_has_children: goal `{goal}` already has child goals and cannot be assigned a parent; goals support only one layer of child goals
texts.goal_id_length: goal_id must contain between 1 and {max} bytes
texts.own_parent: goal cannot be its own parent
texts.source_mismatch: requested source must match the parent; detach or choose a matching parent
texts.tracking_parent: Private tracking items need a private tracking parent
texts.tracking_can_only_change: Private tracking tools can only change tracking records
texts.tracking_can_only_create: Private tracking tools can only create tracking records
texts.tracking_source_immutable: Private tracking tools cannot change a record's source
texts.tracking_linked_not_shared: Private tracking items are linked, not shared goals
texts.goal_id_format: goal IDs must match `goal_<12 lowercase hex chars>`
texts.briefing_id_format: briefing IDs must match `goal_briefing_<12 lowercase hex chars>`
texts.status_values_tracking: must be `active` or `completed` for a tracking lifecycle transition
texts.status_must_be: Status must be active or completed.
texts.edit_needs_field: at least one field must be provided for edit
texts.status_not_editable: status is not editable here - use the set_status action
texts.category_user_only: category applies to user goals only; tracked work items do not carry one
texts.user_goal_exists_for_tracking: goal `{goal}` is a user goal and already represents this responsibility; do not create a tracking record or subgoal for its check-ins - attach crons to the existing goal (owner `goal:<goal-slug>`) and log progress with `user_goal.create_entry`
texts.current_state_ops: current_state is available only for create, update, add_entry, or edit_entry
texts.unavailable_in_run: {tool} is unavailable in this run: propose goal changes in your submitted step output — deterministic downstream steps own accepted goal mutations. Use list/search/view here for grounding.
texts.watch_missing: This tracked item has no watch, so set `watch` together with `requested`.
texts.watch_user_requested: The user asked for this item's watch, so it stays as they set it.
texts.watch_sender_email: goal watch sender must be an email address
texts.watch_ids: goal watch ids must be non-empty, without surrounding whitespace or NUL
texts.watch_note: goal watch note must have text and no NUL
texts.escalation_due_at: goal escalation due_at is not a valid RFC 3339 timestamp
texts.escalation_stored_invalid: invalid stored goal escalation: condition and due_at must be non-empty
texts.follow_up_at_invalid: follow_up_at must be an RFC 3339 timestamp
texts.follow_up_needs_connection: A follow-up needs a coordination conversation
